Subject: Questions on Order Form – billing floor vs. cap semantics

Lukas —

Thanks again for walking us through the order form yesterday. Our procurement team reviewed Exhibit B and has two items we need you to confirm before we proceed to legal redlines:

1) Floor interpretation: the Exhibit references a "monthly billing floor" (minimum charge) measured on committed token units. If usage falls below the floor, Helix is charged the floor amount. Can you confirm whether the floor is calculated against billed tokens after caching/prefix deductions, or against raw generated tokens?

2) Cap/fallback: Exhibit B also defines a soft cap with a separate overage rate above the cap. If we trigger the cap, is the fallback model/rate applied per-request or on a weekly aggregate? We need the language tightened for our internal cost forecasting.

I've attached our current version of the Order Form (Helix_OrderForm_v2.pdf) with highlights. We'd prefer to get a single redline that (a) clarifies the floor calculation, (b) defines the cap fallback mechanics, and (c) adds an ops safeguard for sudden burst billing. Can someone on your side propose wording?

Best,

Lukas / Kim —

Draft suggested redline for Exhibit B (pull quote we can paste into the order form):

"Exhibit B — Billing Floor and Usage Cap (proposed wording)

1. Billing Floor (Minimum Monthly Charge). For purposes of this Agreement, the "Billing Floor" for a given month shall be calculated based on Billed Token Units, defined as the number of tokens invoiced after application of Redwood's production caching and prefix-deduction mechanisms ("Billed Token Units"). Customer shall be charged the greater of (a) the actual charges for Billed Token Units consumed during the month and (b) the Billing Floor amount specified in the Order Form.

2. Usage Cap and Fallback. The "Usage Cap" is a threshold defined in the Order Form. If Customer's Billed Token Units for a billing day exceed the Usage Cap, Redwood may automatically route traffic to a compatible fallback model or tier for the remainder of that billing day. The fallback will be applied on a per-day aggregate basis (UTC), and overage billing will be calculated pro rata based on the aggregate excess Billed Token Units for that UTC day.

3. Burst Safeguard and Notification. In the event of a sudden spike in usage that exceeds the Usage Cap by more than 150% in a single UTC day, Redwood will (a) attempt to notify the Customer within one hour of detection, (b) limit routing to fallback tiers to preserve overall platform stability, and (c) apply a discretionary one-time credit for clearly demonstrable measurement anomalies at Redwood's reasonable discretion.

-- end redline --

Notes:
- Legal intentionally references Billed Token Units (post-cache) to keep operational caching behavior out of dispute over invoicing.
- The per-day aggregate application for fallback simplifies reconciliation vs per-request routing.

I've attached a docx with tracked changes (ExhibitB_redline_v1.docx). If we want to make fallback hourly instead of daily, finance needs to simulate billing permutations — Kim?

Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ExhibitB_redline_v1.docx (tracked changes)"

Agree with Laura's draft. A couple of finance notes to consider before we send to Helix: 

- If fallback is per-day aggregate (UTC), we should confirm whether Helix wants calendar day or rolling-24h for forecasting. Per-day is far simpler to bill, but can cause edge-case double-counting for customers in APAC. Region is US for Helix, so UTC/day should be fine.
- Measurement: using Billed Token Units (post-cache) reduces disputes and is our current practice, but we should enumerate "production caching and prefix-deduction mechanisms" in the billing playbook (ops doc) and not in the contract to avoid tech-level churn in contract text.
- Credit policy: agree with a discretionary credit for measurement anomalies, but we should limit to a single credit per 12-month period unless otherwise escalated. Suggested contract sentence: "Discretionary credits under this Section 3 shall be limited to one occurrence per twelve (12) month period unless otherwise agreed in writing."

If that's acceptable, I suggest we send Laura's redline + a short bullet summary for Helix procurement so they can circulate to their financial forecasting team.

-- Kim
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
